rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Animals are classified by level of organisation (cellular to organ system), body symmetry (asymmetry, radial, bilateral), body cavity (acoelom, pseudocoelom, coelom), and segmentation. The animal kingdom spans 9 major phyla from Porifera (cellular level) to Chordata (organ system level).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Body cavity: Acoelom (no cavity) / Pseudocoelom (partly lined) / Coelom (fully mesoderm-lined)
Symmetry: Asymmetry (Porifera) / Radial (Cnidaria, Echinodermata) / Bilateral (Platyhelminthes onward)
Chordate features: notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Acoelomates have NO body cavity; pseudocoelomates have a cavity not fully lined by mesoderm; coelomates have a fully mesoderm-lined cavity.  ·  Cnidaria are radial (adult) but their larvae may be bilateral; echinoderms are radial in adults but bilateral in larvae (secondary radial symmetry).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the 9-phylum list with one class each and the body-cavity types.  ·  The 4 chordate features are a very common short-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Porifera (sponges): Sycon, Spongaria — cellular organisation, radial/asymmetric.  ·  Cnidaria: Hydra, Aurelia (jellyfish) — radial symmetry, tissue level, cnidocytes.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Segmentation (metamerism) is seen in annelids, arthropods, and chordates — NOT in sponges or cnidarians.  ·  Porifera (sponges) have a cellular level of organisation (no true tissues); Cnidaria have tissue-level organisation.

rows.text: 9 phyla: P-C-P-N-A-A-M-E-C (Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, Chordata).  ·  Chordate = C-D-P-P (Chordate, Dorsal nerve, Pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail).

rows.text: Levels of organisation  ·  Body symmetry  ·  Body cavity types  ·  Segmentation

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Levels: cellular (Porifera) → tissue (Cnidaria) → organ system (higher).  ·  Body cavity: acoelom, pseudocoelom, coelom.  ·  Symmetry: asymmetry, radial, bilateral.  ·  Segmentation in Annelida, Arthropoda, Chordata.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Arthropoda is the most diverse animal phylum (insects, crustaceans, arachnids, myriapods).  ·  Porifera are the simplest animals with a cellular (no tissue) level of organisation.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: List the animal phyla with diagnostic features.  ·  State the four chordate features.  ·  Differentiate the vertebrate classes.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Explain radial vs bilateral symmetry.  ·  State the 4 chordate features.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Platyhelminthes: Planaria (flatworm) — acoelomate, bilateral, dorso-ventrally flattened.  ·  Nematoda: Ascaris (roundworm) — pseudocoelomate, cylindrical.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The body cavity fully lined by mesoderm is called: → C  ·  Cnidaria shows what type of symmetry? → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Levels of organisation: cellular (sponges) → tissue → organ system (most animals).  ·  Body symmetry: asymmetry (sponges), radial (cnidarians, echinoderms), bilateral (most animals).  ·  Body cavity: acoelom (no cavity, flatworms), pseudocoelom (partly lined, nematodes), coelom (fully lined, most higher animals).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: 9 animal phyla  ·  Chordate features  ·  Vertebrate classes

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Diagnostic features  ·  9 phyla: Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, Chordata.  ·  Chordate: notochord, dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Vertebrate classes: Pisces, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia.  ·  Nematodes (roundworms) are pseudocoelomates; Annelida are coelomates.  ·  All chordates have a notochord at some stage; in vertebrates it is replaced by the vertebral column.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Annelida: Pheretima (earthworm) — coelomate, segmented.  ·  Arthropoda: Insecta (cockroach), Crustacea (prawn), Arachnida (scorpion).  ·  Mollusca: snail, octopus, clam — mantle + foot.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Echinodermata: starfish — radial symmetry (adult), water-vascular system.  ·  Chordata: Pisces, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia.  ·  Differentiate acoelom/pseudocoelom/coelom with phylum examples.
